messages.author: b6447277b7989ef2
messages.subject: Troubleshoot Tutorial
parts:
Hello, 

I've been having difficulty finding an answer to the following question. I've been following the GWAS-by-subtraction tutorial closely (https://rpubs.com/MichelNivard/565885), using the same input and code. But at "Run the SEM model without SNPs" stage, the output after my usermodel command appears different from the tutorial. 

After following the tutorial to generate LDSCoutput, I used the following code to run an SEM model without SNPs:

>load(file="LDSCoutputCogNonCog.RData")
>model<-'C=~NA*EA + start(0.4)*CP
        NC=~NA*EA
         
         NC~~1*NC
         C~~1*C
         C~~0*NC

         CP ~~ 0*EA
         CP~~0*CP
         EA~~0*EA'

>output<-usermodel(LDSCoutput,estimation="DWLS",model=model)

[1] "Running primary model"

[1] "Calculating model chi-square"

[1] "Calculating CFI"

[1] "Calculating Standardized Results"

[1] "Calculating SRMR"

elapsed 

  1.021 

[1] "Model fit statistics are all printed as NA as you have specified a fully saturated model (i.e., df = 0)"

> output

$modelfit

   chisq df p_chisq AIC CFI SRMR

df    NA  0      NA  NA  NA   NA


$results

  lhs op rhs Unstand_Est          Unstand_SE STD_Genotype    STD_Genotype_SE

1   C =~  EA   0.2298708 0.00535873579410737    0.6859947 0.0159918750218382

2  NC =~  EA   0.2438145 0.00436859738964419    0.7276065 0.0130370419171318

    STD_All  p_value

1 0.6859947 < 5e-300

2 0.7276065 < 5e-300

In the tutorial, there are more variables listed in output$results, and SRMR is calculated (see below). Can you please help me understanding what is missing here?



Thank you so much for your kind and patient help

Joe

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Troubleshoot Tutorial
parts:
Hi Joe, 

Thanks for raising this. Their was an update to the merge functions that the package uses that was removing fixed parameters (e.g., C~~C); I've put in a fix so if you redownload Genomic SEM, restart R, and rerun your code your output should mirror what is shown on the tutorial page. This is with the exception that SRMR should be printed as NA as you see in your output. This was a more recent update to not print SRMR for fully saturated models,  such as a GWAS-by-subtraction model, as these model will perfectly fit the data, in which case model fit statistics should not be reported. 

Best, 
  Andrew
